memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'Joseph is a fruitful vine, a fruitful vine near a spring, whose branches climb over a wall. With bitterness archers attacked him; they shot at him with hostility. But his bow remained steady, his strong arms stayed limber, because of the hand of the Mighty One of Jacob, because of the Shepherd, the Rock of Israel.'" — Gen 49:22-24 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Jacob's word over Joseph is the longest and warmest of them all, and it names both sides of his life honestly.

The archers were real. "With bitterness archers attacked him; they shot at him with hostility." Jacob does not pretend Joseph's life was easy. The pit, the slave market, Potiphar's wife, the prison, the forgetting — every one of those was an arrow.

And yet, "his bow remained steady."

But read the reason carefully, because it is the whole point: "because of the hand of the Mighty One of Jacob, because of the Shepherd, the Rock of Israel." Joseph's steadiness was not a personality trait. It was God's hand on him.

That is enormously freeing. We look at people who stayed faithful through terrible things and assume they were made of stronger material than us. Jacob says no — it was God who held them.

Notice too that the vine is fruitful *near a spring*. Fruitfulness comes from being planted near a water source, not from trying harder. Jesus said it plainly: remain in me, for apart from me you can do nothing (Jn 15:5).

Whatever arrows are coming, your steadiness will come from the same hand.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What arrows have come at you, and how have you weathered them?
2. Do you credit your steadiness to yourself or to God's hand?
3. Are you planted near the spring, or trying to be fruitful on your own?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that Joseph's steadiness came from Your hand and mine can too. Keep me planted near the spring, and hold me steady under whatever comes. Amen.
